column2:
dazzle(v./n.)使目眩、使讚嘆、耀眼的光
dazzling(adj.)耀眼的、令人驚豔的
be dazzled by 被……迷住
dazzle the audience 令觀眾驚豔
The audience was dazzled by the dancers' amazing performance.
(觀眾被舞者們精采的表演深深吸引。)
The bright headlights of the truck dazzled me for a moment.
(卡車刺眼的大燈讓我一時睜不開眼。)

deafen(v.)使聾、震耳欲聾
deaf(adj.)聾的
deafening(adj.)震耳欲聾的
deafening noise 震耳欲聾的噪音
deafening silence 令人難堪的沉默
The crowd's cheers deafened us when the team scored the winning goal.
(球隊踢進致勝球時，群眾的歡呼聲震耳欲聾。)
Working near the loud machines without earplugs may deafen you.
(在吵雜機器旁工作不戴耳塞可能會讓你聽力受損。)

decisive(adj.)決定性的、果斷的
decide(v.)決定
decision(n.)決定
decisively(adv.)果斷地
decisive moment 關鍵時刻
decisive victory 決定性的勝利
A good leader must be decisive in times of crisis.
(好的領導者在危機時刻必須果斷。)
His goal in the final minute proved decisive.
(他在最後一分鐘的進球成為致勝關鍵。)

dedication(n.)奉獻、專注、獻詞
dedicate(v.)奉獻、致力於
dedicated(adj.)專注的、盡心盡力的
dedication to 對……的奉獻
hard work and dedication 努力與奉獻
The nurse was praised for her dedication to her patients.
(那位護理師因為對病人的盡心奉獻而受到讚揚。)
Becoming a professional pianist requires years of dedication.
(成為職業鋼琴家需要多年的專注投入。)

deduct(v.)扣除、減去
deduction(n.)扣除、推論
deductible(adj.)可扣除的
deduct points 扣分
deduct from 從……中扣除
The teacher will deduct points if you hand in your homework late.
(如果你遲交作業，老師會扣分。)
Taxes are automatically deducted from his monthly salary.
(稅金會自動從他的月薪中扣除。)

deem(v.)認為、視為
(無詞性變化)
deem it necessary 認為有必要
be deemed (to be) 被視為
The building was deemed unsafe after the earthquake.
(這棟建築在地震後被認定為不安全。)
The principal will take whatever action he deems necessary.
(校長將採取他認為必要的任何措施。)

default(n./v.)預設值、違約、不履行
(無詞性變化)
by default 預設地、因對方缺席
default setting 預設設定
The phone's default language is English, but you can change it.
(這支手機的預設語言是英文，但你可以更改。)
The company defaulted on its loan and went bankrupt.
(這家公司拖欠貸款後破產了。)

defect(n./v.)缺陷、瑕疵、叛逃
defective(adj.)有缺陷的
defector(n.)叛逃者
birth defect 先天缺陷
product defect 產品瑕疵
The company recalled thousands of cars because of a defect in the brakes.
(由於煞車有瑕疵，這家公司召回了數千輛汽車。)
During the Cold War, some scientists defected to the West.
(冷戰期間，有些科學家叛逃到西方國家。)

defiance(n.)違抗、蔑視、反抗
defy(v.)違抗、蔑視
defiant(adj.)違抗的
in defiance of 不顧、違抗
act of defiance 反抗行為
The students held the protest in defiance of the school's ban.
(學生們不顧學校的禁令舉行抗議。)
He raised his fist as an act of defiance.
(他舉起拳頭表示反抗。)

definitive(adj.)決定性的、最權威的
definite(adj.)明確的
definitively(adv.)決定性地
definitive answer 確切的答覆
definitive guide 權威指南
Scientists have not yet found a definitive answer to the question.
(科學家尚未找到這個問題的確切答案。)
This book is considered the definitive guide to Taiwanese birds.
(這本書被視為台灣鳥類最權威的指南。)

dental(adj.)牙齒的、牙科的
dentist(n.)牙醫
dental care 牙齒保健
dental floss 牙線
Good dental care can prevent many problems later in life.
(良好的牙齒保健能預防日後許多問題。)
Using dental floss every day helps keep your gums healthy.
(每天使用牙線有助於保持牙齦健康。)

deplete(v.)耗盡、使枯竭
depletion(n.)耗盡、枯竭
deplete resources 耗盡資源
ozone depletion 臭氧層破洞
Overfishing has seriously depleted fish populations in the ocean.
(過度捕撈已嚴重耗盡海洋中的魚群數量。)
Human activities are depleting the earth's natural resources.
(人類的活動正在耗盡地球的自然資源。)

deprive(v.)剝奪、使喪失
deprivation(n.)剝奪、匱乏
deprived(adj.)貧困的、被剝奪的
deprive sb. of 剝奪某人的……
sleep deprivation 睡眠不足
Too much homework deprives students of time to rest.
(過多的作業剝奪了學生休息的時間。)
Sleep deprivation can affect your memory and concentration.
(睡眠不足會影響你的記憶力和專注力。)

descent(n.)下降、血統、出身
descend(v.)下降
descendant(n.)後代
of ... descent ……血統的
steep descent 陡坡
The plane began its descent into Taoyuan Airport.
(飛機開始下降準備降落桃園機場。)
She is of Japanese descent but grew up in Taiwan.
(她有日本血統，但在台灣長大。)

despise(v.)鄙視、看不起
despicable(adj.)可鄙的
despise sb. for 因……鄙視某人
openly despise 公然鄙視
She despises people who lie to get what they want.
(她鄙視那些為達目的而說謊的人。)
Don't despise others just because they are poor.
(不要只因為別人貧窮就看不起他們。)

destined(adj.)命中注定的、預定前往的
destiny(n.)命運
destination(n.)目的地
be destined to 注定要
destined for 開往……的、注定……
With her talent, she seems destined to become a great writer.
(憑她的天分，她似乎注定會成為偉大的作家。)
The ship was destined for Japan.
(這艘船預定駛往日本。)

detach(v.)分開、拆下
detached(adj.)分開的、超然的
detachment(n.)分離、超然
detach from 從……分離
detached house 獨棟住宅
Please detach the form and return it to your teacher.
(請撕下這張表格交給你的老師。)
He tries to detach himself from his emotions when making decisions.
(他做決定時會試著讓自己不受情緒影響。)

detain(v.)拘留、扣留、耽擱
detention(n.)拘留、課後留校
detainee(n.)被拘留者
be detained by 被……拘留
detain for questioning 拘留問訊
The suspect was detained by the police for questioning.
(嫌犯被警方拘留問訊。)
I'm sorry I'm late; I was detained by a meeting.
(抱歉我遲到了，我被一個會議耽擱了。)

detention(n.)拘留、課後留校
detain(v.)拘留
detention center 拘留所
get detention 被罰留校
He got detention for talking during the exam.
(他因為考試時講話而被罰留校。)
The men were held in a detention center for several days.
(那些男子被關在拘留所好幾天。)

deter(v.)阻止、威懾
deterrent(n.)威懾力量、嚇阻物
deterrence(n.)嚇阻
deter sb. from 阻止某人做……
deter crime 遏止犯罪
Heavy fines are meant to deter people from littering.
(高額罰款是為了嚇阻人們亂丟垃圾。)
Nothing could deter her from pursuing her dream.
(沒有什麼能阻止她追求夢想。)

detergent(n.)清潔劑、洗衣精
(無詞性變化)
laundry detergent 洗衣精
dish detergent 洗碗精
Add a cup of laundry detergent before starting the washing machine.
(啟動洗衣機前先加入一杯洗衣精。)
Some detergents contain chemicals that pollute rivers.
(有些清潔劑含有會汙染河川的化學物質。)

devour(v.)狼吞虎嚥、吞噬、如飢似渴地閱讀
(無詞性變化)
devour a meal 狼吞虎嚥地吃一頓
devour books 如飢似渴地看書
The hungry boys devoured the whole pizza in five minutes.
(那群飢餓的男孩五分鐘就把整個披薩吃光了。)
She devoured every Harry Potter book as soon as it came out.
(每本《哈利波特》一出版，她就迫不及待地讀完。)

diabetes(n.)糖尿病
diabetic(adj./n.)糖尿病的、糖尿病患者
type 2 diabetes 第二型糖尿病
risk of diabetes 糖尿病風險
Drinking too many sugary drinks increases the risk of diabetes.
(喝太多含糖飲料會增加罹患糖尿病的風險。)
People with diabetes need to check their blood sugar regularly.
(糖尿病患者需要定期檢查血糖。)

dictate(v.)口述、命令、支配
dictation(n.)聽寫、口述
dictator(n.)獨裁者
dictate a letter 口述信件
dictate terms 規定條件
The manager dictated a letter to his secretary.
(經理向祕書口述了一封信。)
The weather will dictate whether we hold the event outdoors.
(天氣將決定我們是否在戶外舉辦活動。)

dictation(n.)聽寫、口述
dictate(v.)口述
take dictation 做聽寫、記錄口述
dictation test 聽寫測驗
We have an English dictation test every Friday.
(我們每週五都有英文聽寫測驗。)
The secretary took dictation during the meeting.
(祕書在會議中記錄口述內容。)

dictator(n.)獨裁者
dictatorship(n.)獨裁政權
dictatorial(adj.)獨裁的
military dictator 軍事獨裁者
overthrow a dictator 推翻獨裁者
The people finally overthrew the dictator after years of protests.
(經過多年的抗議，人民終於推翻了獨裁者。)
The dictator controlled the media and silenced his critics.
(那名獨裁者控制媒體並壓制批評者。)

dictatorship(n.)獨裁政權、專政
dictator(n.)獨裁者
military dictatorship 軍事獨裁
under a dictatorship 在獨裁統治下
The country was ruled by a military dictatorship for decades.
(這個國家數十年來由軍事獨裁政權統治。)
Freedom of speech is often limited under a dictatorship.
(在獨裁統治下，言論自由經常受到限制。)

diesel(n.)柴油、柴油引擎
(無詞性變化)
diesel engine 柴油引擎
diesel fuel 柴油
Many old trucks run on diesel and cause serious air pollution.
(許多老舊卡車使用柴油，造成嚴重空氣汙染。)
The city plans to replace its diesel buses with electric ones.
(市政府計畫把柴油公車換成電動公車。)

differentiate(v.)區別、區分
differentiation(n.)區別、分化
different(adj.)不同的
differentiate between 區分
differentiate A from B 把 A 與 B 區分開來
Young children cannot always differentiate between fantasy and reality.
(年幼的孩子不一定能區分幻想與現實。)
What differentiates this phone from others is its long battery life.
(這支手機與眾不同之處在於電池續航力很長。)

diplomacy(n.)外交、交際手腕
diplomat(n.)外交官
diplomatic(adj.)外交的、圓滑的
international diplomacy 國際外交
with diplomacy 圓融地
The conflict between the two countries was solved through diplomacy.
(兩國間的衝突透過外交途徑解決了。)
She handled the angry customer with great diplomacy.
(她非常圓融地處理了那位生氣的顧客。)

directive(n.)指令、命令
direct(v.)指揮、指示
direction(n.)方向、指示
issue a directive 發布指令
government directive 政府指令
The school received a directive from the Ministry of Education.
(學校收到教育部的一項指令。)
All staff must follow the new safety directive.
(所有員工都必須遵守新的安全指令。)

disable(v.)使失去能力、使傷殘、停用
disabled(adj.)身心障礙的、被停用的
disability(n.)身心障礙
disable a function 停用功能
disabled parking 身障停車位
You can disable the notifications in the phone's settings.
(你可以在手機的設定中停用通知。)
The accident disabled him, but he never gave up on his dreams.
(這場意外使他身體傷殘，但他從未放棄夢想。)

disastrous(adj.)災難性的、極糟的
disaster(n.)災難
disastrously(adv.)災難性地
disastrous effect 災難性的影響
disastrous result 極糟的結果
The typhoon had a disastrous effect on the farmers' crops.
(颱風對農民的作物造成了災難性的影響。)
Cheating on the exam could lead to disastrous results.
(考試作弊可能導致極為嚴重的後果。)

disbelief(n.)不相信、懷疑
disbelieve(v.)不相信
in disbelief 不敢置信地
shake one's head in disbelief 不可置信地搖頭
She stared at her exam results in disbelief.
(她不敢置信地盯著自己的考試成績。)
The fans watched in disbelief as their team lost the final.
(球迷們難以置信地看著自己的隊伍輸掉決賽。)

discard(v./n.)丟棄、拋棄、被拋棄之物
(無詞性變化)
discard old clothes 丟棄舊衣
discard a theory 揚棄理論
Please discard used batteries in the special recycling bins.
(請把用過的電池丟進專用的回收桶。)
Scientists discarded the old theory after new evidence was found.
(發現新證據後，科學家們揚棄了舊理論。)

discharge(n./v.)排放、出院、解雇、履行
(無詞性變化)
be discharged from hospital 出院
discharge waste 排放廢棄物
My grandmother was discharged from the hospital yesterday.
(我奶奶昨天出院了。)
The factory was fined for discharging waste into the river.
(這間工廠因將廢棄物排入河中而被罰款。)

disciple(n.)門徒、追隨者、弟子
discipleship(n.)門徒身分
loyal disciple 忠實的追隨者
disciple of ……的信徒
Confucius had many disciples who spread his teachings.
(孔子有許多傳播他學說的弟子。)
He is a devoted disciple of the famous chef.
(他是那位名廚忠實的追隨者。)

disciplinary(adj.)紀律的、懲戒的、學科的
discipline(n./v.)紀律、懲戒
disciplinary action 懲處
interdisciplinary 跨學科的
The school will take disciplinary action against students who bully others.
(學校將對霸凌他人的學生採取懲處措施。)
The project requires an interdisciplinary approach combining science and art.
(這個專題需要結合科學與藝術的跨學科方法。)

disclosure(n.)揭露、透露、公開
disclose(v.)揭露、透露
public disclosure 公開揭露
disclosure of information 資訊揭露
The disclosure of personal data without permission is illegal.
(未經允許揭露個人資料是違法的。)
Companies must make full disclosure of their financial situation.
(公司必須完整公開其財務狀況。)

discomfort(n./v.)不適、不舒服、使不安
comfort(n.)舒適
uncomfortable(adj.)不舒服的
physical discomfort 身體不適
cause discomfort 造成不適
You may feel some discomfort after the dental treatment.
(牙齒治療後你可能會感到一些不適。)
He shifted in his seat, clearly in discomfort.
(他在座位上挪動身子，顯然很不自在。)

discreet(adj.)謹慎的、低調的
discretion(n.)謹慎、斟酌權
discreetly(adv.)謹慎地
be discreet about 對……保密、低調
discreet inquiry 私下打聽
Please be discreet and don't tell anyone about the surprise party.
(請保密，別告訴任何人這個驚喜派對。)
She gave him a discreet signal to stop talking.
(她不動聲色地示意他別再說了。)

disgrace(n./v.)恥辱、丟臉、使蒙羞
disgraceful(adj.)可恥的
in disgrace 丟臉地、失寵
bring disgrace on 使……蒙羞
The politician resigned in disgrace after the scandal.
(那位政治人物在醜聞後丟臉地辭職了。)
His cheating brought disgrace on the whole team.
(他的作弊行為讓整個隊伍蒙羞。)

dismay(n./v.)沮喪、驚愕、使灰心
dismayed(adj.)沮喪的、驚愕的
to one's dismay 令某人沮喪的是
in dismay 驚慌地
To our dismay, the concert was canceled because of the typhoon.
(令我們沮喪的是，演唱會因颱風取消了。)
She looked at the broken vase in dismay.
(她驚慌地看著破掉的花瓶。)

dispensable(adj.)非必要的、可有可無的
indispensable(adj.)不可或缺的
dispense(v.)分配、省去
dispensable item 非必需品
be considered dispensable 被視為可有可無
In a tight budget, eating out is a dispensable expense.
(在預算吃緊時，外食是可以省下的開銷。)
No member of our team is dispensable; everyone plays an important role.
(我們隊上沒有人是可有可無的，每個人都扮演重要角色。)

dispense(v.)分配、發放、配藥
dispenser(n.)自動販賣機、分配器
dispensable(adj.)非必要的
dispense with 省去、免除
water dispenser 飲水機
The machine dispenses hot and cold drinks.
(這台機器供應冷熱飲料。)
Let's dispense with the formalities and get straight to the point.
(我們省去那些客套，直接切入重點吧。)

disposable(adj./n.)用完即丟的、可支配的、拋棄式用品
dispose(v.)處理、丟棄
disposal(n.)處置
disposable cups 免洗杯
disposable income 可支配所得
Many shops no longer provide disposable plastic straws.
(許多店家已不再提供一次性塑膠吸管。)
People with more disposable income tend to travel more.
(可支配所得較多的人往往比較常旅行。)

disposal(n.)處置、處理、支配權
dispose(v.)處理、丟棄
waste disposal 廢棄物處理
at one's disposal 任某人支配
Proper waste disposal is important for protecting the environment.
(妥善處理廢棄物對保護環境很重要。)
The library has many resources at your disposal.
(圖書館有許多資源可供你使用。)

dispose(v.)處理、丟棄、使傾向
disposal(n.)處置
disposable(adj.)用完即丟的
dispose of 處理、丟棄
be disposed to 傾向於
Please dispose of your trash properly after the picnic.
(野餐後請妥善處理你的垃圾。)
The government is looking for a safe way to dispose of nuclear waste.
(政府正在尋找安全處理核廢料的方法。)

dissent(n.)異議、不同意見
dissenter(n.)持異議者
dissenting(adj.)持異議的
voice dissent 表達異議
political dissent 政治異議
In a democracy, people are free to express dissent.
(在民主社會中，人們可以自由表達異議。)
The decision was passed with little dissent.
(這項決議幾乎沒有異議就通過了。)

distraction(n.)分心、使分心的事物、消遣
distract(v.)使分心
distracted(adj.)分心的
without distraction 不受干擾地
drive sb. to distraction 使某人心煩意亂
Smartphones can be a big distraction when you are studying.
(讀書時，智慧型手機可能是很大的干擾。)
I need a quiet place to work without distraction.
(我需要一個不受干擾的安靜地方工作。)

distress(n./v.)痛苦、苦惱、危難、使苦惱
distressed(adj.)苦惱的
distressing(adj.)令人痛苦的
in distress 處於危難中、苦惱
distress signal 求救信號
The coast guard rescued a fishing boat in distress.
(海巡人員救援了一艘遇險的漁船。)
The news of the accident caused great distress to the family.
(這起意外的消息讓那個家庭非常痛苦。)

disturbance(n.)干擾、騷亂、失調
disturb(v.)打擾
disturbing(adj.)令人不安的
cause a disturbance 引起騷動
sleep disturbance 睡眠障礙
The noisy neighbors caused a disturbance late at night.
(吵鬧的鄰居深夜引起了騷動。)
Construction work nearby is a constant disturbance to our classes.
(附近的施工持續干擾我們上課。)

diversify(v.)使多樣化、多元發展
diversity(n.)多樣性
diverse(adj.)多樣的
diversification(n.)多樣化
diversify the economy 使經濟多元化
diversify into 擴展業務至
The farm diversified by opening a café for visitors.
(這座農場透過為遊客開設咖啡廳來多元經營。)
Countries that rely on one industry should diversify their economies.
(仰賴單一產業的國家應該讓經濟多元化。)
